title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops, ROPE optimization, KV-batching and scheduler integration
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: Reduce tail latency and improve throughput for long-context generative workloads by upgrading the attention implementation and integrating it with the scheduler and KV cache batching paths. This change brings FlashAttentionV2 kernels upstream, adds fused query/key/value + output ops where possible, and exposes ROPE/rotary precomputation optimizations. Also integrates KV-batching hooks into the continuous-batching scheduler so that cached KV regions are coalesced more aggressively.

What this PR does: - Replace the legacy attention path with an opt-in FlashAttentionV2 backend and add a runtime switch for fallback. - Implement fused projection+softmax+matmul kernels for common dims (head_dim 64/128) to reduce kernel launches. - ROPE (rotary) optimization: precompute and cache rotary embeddings per block and add a fast path for common rotary angle alignments. - KV-batching integration: extend continuous batching scheduler to form batches by matching KV cache compatibility (model version, key schema, seq alignment) and emit coalesced KV dispatches. - Scheduling hooks: add tracing points and backpressure signals so the scheduler can prioritize low-latency tails while still aggregating for throughput. - API/compat: expose a config flag (attention.backend) and new perf knobs (kv.batching.window_ms, fused_ops.enabled) in model config.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for new kernels and fallback - [x] Regression tests against existing model zoo - [x] Microbenchmarks (latency/throughput) - [x] End-to-end smoke tests on dedicated and hosted modes - [x] Docs/upgrade notes

Performance summary: On a mix of summarization and chat workloads (seq_len up to 8k) we see ~1.6x median throughput and 20-40% P95 latency reduction for long-context batched workloads; in low-concurrency single-client tails we observe a 10-15% latency improvement due to reduced kernel-launch overhead. KV-heavy rerun benchmarks showed up to 2.1x effective throughput when KV-batching coalescing fired. Memory overhead: negligible for typical head sizes; ROPE precomputation adds ~0.5% to peak GPU memory for tested models.

Compatibility notes: The new backend is gated behind attention.backend: flashattnv2 and falls back to legacy implementation automatically for unsupported op sizes or hardware. We added runtime checks and telemetry to detect fallback rates. If fallback > 5% for a model over a 1-hour window, we emit a warning and revert to legacy by default for that model to avoid regressions.

Release notes: Opt-in FlashAttentionV2 backend with fused ops and ROPE optimizations. KV-batching and scheduler integration improve throughput for KV-heavy long-context workloads.

Related: ENG-2345 (attention upgrade), ENG-2410 (scheduler KV batching integration), SUP-4120 (customer impact investigation), previous PRs: pr-134210, pr-128999, pr-113457.
